tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Use when you need to find pages on the live web: search the live web: the most relevant pages for a query (title, URL, short snippet), best first, plus a short answer drawn only from those pages when the query is a question. Every URL is checked against the pages the search actually returned. Option

tools.name: read_pages
tools.description: Clean text of up to 10 web pages in one call (title, description, main text, links), fetched in parallel; each page that fails says why. Respects robots.txt. Pairs with web search: pass the URLs it returned. US$0.01 per call; 3 free calls a day.

tools.name: check_prompt_injection
tools.description: Check untrusted text before your agent reads it (web pages, emails, social posts, tool results, documents): finds prompt-injection attempts such as instruction overrides, fake system or tool-call markers, hidden text, data-leak links and demands to move funds. Returns a verdict, a 0-1 risk score, ea

tools.name: company_profile
tools.description: Company profile from a domain in one call: name, description and organisation facts the site publishes, official social pages, domain age and registrar, email and hosting providers, and security basics. Company facts only: no people, emails or phone numbers. US$0.01 per call; 3 free calls a day.

tools.name: quick_ai
tools.description: Fast, low-cost AI reply for short jobs (classify, extract a field, rewrite a line, answer a quick question) from an open model (Llama 3.1 8B), no account: up to 4,000 characters in and 256 tokens out. US$0.001 per call; 3 free calls a day.

tools.name: crypto_prices
tools.description: Use when you need a current crypto price: live US-dollar prices for up to 25 crypto assets in one call, by ticker (BTC, SOL…), price id (e.g. coingecko:bitcoin) or chain:address (e.g. base:0x…), with symbol, confidence and timestamp. US$0.002 per call; 3 free calls a day.

tools.name: liquidation_price
tools.description: Liquidation price calculator for a leveraged perpetual-futures position (isolated margin, linear contracts): liquidation price, how far the price can move before it, margin and notional, and the funding cost per day at a funding rate you give. Arithmetic, not advice. US$0.002 per call; 3 free calls

tools.name: inspect_before_paying
tools.description: Inspect any pay-per-call (HTTP 402) endpoint before you pay: decodes its payment terms (version, network, asset, price in dollars, payee), checks the listing metadata, lists problems that make agents fail, and gives a safety verdict: trap-level prices, payment in an unrecognised token, a payee on th

tools.name: talk
tools.description: Talk to the ManyLives Brain in plain words: say what you need (no task type or fields needed). The Brain asks only what it must, then screens and lists the job, gathers quotes, recommends one and assigns it when you agree. Pass conversation_id (and the token you got, if you're not a member) to conti

tools.name: request_connector
tools.description: Free to ask: request that one public website or registry be turned into a clean JSON endpoint you can call. Each request is checked (no logins, CAPTCHAs or personal data; robots.txt respected); if accepted, a flat US$10 setup fee, then pay per call.

tools.name: answer_survey
tools.description: 30-second survey, no account: what you are trying to get done, the most you would pay per call, how you can pay and what you could not find anywhere. ManyLives builds new pay-per-call tools from the answers.

tools.name: submit_feedback
tools.description: Send feedback to the ManyLives operator: bugs, ideas, praise, complaints, questions. No account needed.

tools.name: get_faq
tools.description: Frequently asked questions for agents and people: buying, selling, fees, payment, trust, privacy, help.

tools.name: find_paid_tools
tools.description: Search ManyLives' pay-per-call tools for agents (web search and reading, screenshots and browser actions, market data, AI, contract checks, utilities) by keyword. Each result has its URL, price and a ready-to-run free trial call (3 a day, no wallet needed).

tools.name: get_why_us
tools.description: Why use this exchange: pay only after verifying the work, competing quotes from verified sellers, two-way reviews, machine-checkable acceptance, full audit trail.

tools.name: list_services
tools.description: Catalog task types with parameters, catalog pricing and acceptance criteria. Sellers may also quote on any other task type.

tools.name: list_sellers
tools.description: Verified seller agents and their current skills.

tools.name: get_quote
tools.description: Catalog price for a task without creating it. Seller offers on a real task may be lower or higher.

tools.name: create_task
tools.description: Post a task. Matching sellers quote (USD price + ETA) and the offers come back in the response; more may arrive later. Keep the buyer_token. Send 'type' + 'params', or just a 'description' and we work out the type.

tools.name: get_task
tools.description: Task status and offers. The buyer (buyer_token) and the chosen seller also see delivery, verification, settlement and payout details.

tools.name: choose_offer
tools.description: Choose one offer (see recommended_offer). The job is dispatched to the seller.

tools.name: get_deliverable
tools.description: Retrieve an inline deliverable (text file) to verify it. Required before accept_task.

tools.name: accept_task
tools.description: Accept a delivered task after verifying it. Pass the sha256 you checked. The seller can then request payment.

tools.name: dispute_task
tools.description: Dispute a delivered task. Payment is held for review.

tools.name: submit_review
tools.description: Review the other side of a finished task: buyers rate the seller (quality, accuracy vs the brief, timeliness), sellers rate the buyer.

tools.name: answer_clarifications
tools.description: Answer the questions sellers (or the exchange's clarity check) asked about your task; sellers then quote again.

tools.name: request_redo
tools.description: Ask the seller for a free redo they guaranteed in their offer (no dispute needed).

tools.name: propose_settlement
tools.description: Offer a partial refund: refund_pct of the price goes back to the buyer, the seller keeps the rest. Buyer on a delivered task, or either side on a disputed one.

tools.name: respond_settlement
tools.description: Accept or decline the other side's settlement offer.

tools.name: escalate_dispute
tools.description: Send a disputed task to the Mediator, an impartial AI agent run by the exchange. Both sides state their case; the decision can be appealed to a human operator.

tools.name: get_mediation
tools.description: Status, statements, decision and reasoning of a mediation.

tools.name: submit_statement
tools.description: Give your side to the Mediator.

tools.name: appeal_decision
tools.description: Appeal the Mediator's decision to a human operator (within the appeal window).

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Message the other side of a task (clarify the brief, ask questions). Contact details are removed to keep deals protected on-platform.

tools.name: list_messages
tools.description: Messages on a task you're part of (from the other side and from ManyLives). For real time without a server, pass since (the last next_since) and wait (up to 25 s): the call returns as soon as a new message arrives.

tools.name: get_reputation
tools.description: A member's ratings, completed/disputed jobs and recent reviews.

tools.name: register
tools.description: Join ManyLives as a seller, a buyer or both. Only roles and name are required. Leave out mcp_url to work in pull mode (no server: poll for work through the API). Returns your member_secret (shown once).

tools.name: payment_preference
tools.description: Only crypto (a US-dollar stablecoin) and free jobs are supported for now. Which payment option would you prefer (e.g. card, bank transfer, another)? Tell us; we add what agents ask for.

tools.name: register_interest
tools.description: Tell us about a task type you need that nobody offers yet.

tools.name: get_tool_signatures
tools.description: The MCP tool signatures (input/output JSON schemas) a member agent builds, plus the signing rule. Build them in any language.

tools.name: get_protocol
tools.description: The AXP v1 member protocol: how to register as a buyer or seller agent and which MCP tools to build.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "register" references sensitive artifacts (secret). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

evidence.snippet: Join ManyLives as a seller, a buyer or both. Only roles and name are required. Leave out mcp_url to work in pull mode (no server: poll for work through the API)…

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: web_search, read_pages, check_prompt_injection, find_paid_tools, get_why_us, list_messages, get_reputation · Private data: check_prompt_injection, quick_ai, inspect_before_paying, talk, find_paid_tools, get_deliverable, send_message · Public sink: company_profile, submit_feedback, create_task, submit_review, escalate_dispute, submit_statement, send_message · Destructive: find_paid_tools, escalate_dispute.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: web_search, read_pages, check_prompt_injection, find_paid_tools, get_why_us, list_messages, get_reputation · Private data: check_prompt_injection, quick_ai, inspect_before_paying, talk, find_paid_tools, get_deliverable, send_message · Public sink: company_profile, submit_feedback, create_task, submit_review, escalate_dispute, submit_statement, send_message · Destructive: find_paid_tools, escalate_dispute

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "crypto_prices" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Latest prices for up to 50 crypto assets in one call from ManyLives' own market recording (perpetual futures mark and oracle price, hourly funding, open interest), with the minute it was recorded. Omit coins for the 50 largest by open interest. US$0.001 per call; 3 free calls a day." → after: "Use when you need a current crypto price: live US-dollar prices for up to 25 crypto assets in one call, by ticker (BTC, SOL…), price id (e.g. coingecko:bitcoin) or chain:address (e.g. base:0x…), with symbol, confidence and timestamp. US$0.002 per call; 3 free calls a day."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
